case_name: Smt.Sunita Jain vs Pawan Kumar Jain
facts_of_case: The parties are in a domestic violence case. The wife filed an appeal against the trial court's decision. The husband did not file a reply to the wife's affidavit. The court is considering whether the filing of an affidavit of disclosure can be directed at the appellate stage.

legal_principles.principle: At the appellate stage, new material cannot be introduced without testing on the touchstone of evidence.
legal_principles.held: The filing of the affidavit of assets and liabilities would amount to bringing in new material which will have to be tested on the touchstone of evidence which will not be permissible at the appellate stage after final adjudication.

legal_principles.principle: The burden lies on the court to ensure that mandatory provisions of law are complied with.
legal_principles.held: After having gone through the decision of learned Single Judge of Bombay High Court (supra) having tested the same on the anvil of Section 24 of Hindu Marriage Act, we prima-facie feel that the said judgment appears to be rendered per incurium the mandatory provisions of Section 24 of Hindu Marriage Act.

outcome.final_order: The impugned orders are quashed and set aside. The Sessions Court is directed to decide the appeals on their own merits in accordance with law.

keywords: Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act
Latin maxim: Nemo judex in causa sua
